metadata.title: FeedCentral - Centralized News Aggregator
metadata.description: A professional RSS feed aggregator built with Next.js, offering a clean, Vercel-like interface to centralize and verify your news sources.

hero.title: Your News,
hero.subtitle: FeedCentral aggregates your trusted RSS sources into a clean, modern interface. Stay informed without the noise.

mission.title: Take Back Control of Your News Feed
mission.description1: In a world of algorithmic feeds and endless scrolling, FeedCentral brings you back to the basics:
mission.description1Highlight: curated, chronological content from sources you trust
mission.description2: We believe that staying informed shouldn't come at the cost of your privacy, attention, or sanity. FeedCentral is built with transparency, simplicity, and user respect at its core.

about.title: About FeedCentral
about.subtitle: The story behind the project and what we stand for

origin.title: Born from Frustration with Modern News
origin.paragraph1: FeedCentral was born out of frustration with the current state of news consumption. Social media algorithms decide what you see, news websites track your every move, and endless scrolling has replaced intentional reading.
origin.paragraph2: I wanted something different: a clean, simple interface that respects your time and privacy. No algorithms deciding what's important, no tracking cookies following you around, no endless scroll designed to trap your attention.
origin.paragraph3: Just news from sources you trust, presented chronologically, without manipulation.

mission.title: Taking Back Control of Your News Feed
mission.paragraph1: FeedCentral's mission is simple: give people control over their news consumption. We believe you should decide which sources to trust, not an algorithm optimized for engagement.
mission.paragraph2: We're committed to transparency, simplicity, and respect for our users. No dark patterns, no hidden tracking, no selling your data. Just a clean interface for reading news from sources you choose.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.description: Open source code, clear privacy policy, and full visibility into how the platform works.

privacy.title: Privacy First
privacy.description: No tracking cookies, no analytics beyond basic usage stats, no selling your data. Ever.

simplicity.title: Simplicity
simplicity.description: A clean, distraction-free interface that respects your time and attention.

chronological.title: Chronological Feeds
chronological.description: Articles appear in the order they're published, not sorted by engagement algorithms.

hobbyProject.title: Built by One Developer, For the Love of It
hobbyProject.paragraph1: FeedCentral is a hobby project built and maintained by a single developer in their spare time. This isn't a venture-backed startup chasing growth metrics or a commercial product optimized for profit.
hobbyProject.paragraph2: It's a passion project born from the belief that news aggregation can be done better, with respect for users rather than exploitation of them.
hobbyProject.paragraph3: There are no promises of features, no guaranteed response times, no SLAs. Just an ongoing effort to build something useful and share it with others who feel the same way about news consumption.

openSource.title: Free to Use, Fork, and Modify
openSource.paragraph1: FeedCentral is open source under the MIT license. You're free to use it, study it, modify it, and even run your own instance if you prefer.
openSource.paragraph2: The official instance at feed.benzoogataga.com is maintained as a public service, but you're not locked in. If you want complete control, you can deploy your own version.

future.title: Building Features That Matter
future.paragraph1: FeedCentral will continue to evolve based on user feedback and the developer's own needs. The focus will always be on features that improve the reading experience and respect user agency.
future.paragraph2: Features like custom RSS sources, advanced search, bookmarking, and content filtering are already implemented or planned. But feature requests are always welcome.
